label: First Vatican Council, Dei Filius Ch. 3…: The Catholic Church is a teaching authority founded by…
locator: ch. 3, para. 5: Deus per Filium suum unigenitum Ecclesiam instituit
interpretation: God instituted the Church through his only-begotten Son and furnished it with manifest marks of its institution 'ut ea tamquam custos et magistra verbi revelati ab omnibus posset agnosci'; the next sentence ('Ad solam enim catholicam Ecclesiam ea pertinent omnia ...') identifies that Church as the Catholic Church. Read as asserting root component (A): there is a God who founded the Catholic Church as a teaching authority ('magistra verbi revelati'). The council asserts this as doctrine; it does not argue it. The statement is weaker than the text: it drops 'through his Son' and the manifest marks, which are recorded in the sibling claims of the same paragraph.
